items.title: Why Intel’s stock is sinking toward its worst drop in two years
items.description: Intel’s PC business is under pressure as memory-chip prices dent demand and as corporate IT teams have less budget for laptops.

items.title: My abusive ex-husband promised $20,000 for our kids’ education. Now he refuses to pay. Is he legally obligated?
items.description: “Before our divorce, my former mother-in-law entrusted him with $20,000 for each of our daughters to invest on their behalf.”

items.title: The midterms are crucial to the future of Social Security — no matter how old you are
items.description: The program is expected to run out of money in the next six years, which is the same amount of time as a senator’s term.

items.description: “Given the size and long-term nature of this gift, we want to make sure the funds are managed prudently.”

items.title: A Starbucks turnaround is brewing — but perhaps not quickly enough

items.title: Sandisk sees revenue nearly quintuple — and a stock split is on the way

items.title: ‘Fancy cars hold no appeal’: We have a 99% chance of outliving our life savings. Why not spend, spend, spend?
items.description: “I’m 68, she’s 74, and we’re both in good health. We married later in life and have no children.”

items.title: My wife cried when I found out she had only $80,000 in her 401(k). I have $2.2 million. Am I wrong to be shocked?
items.description: “When I brought up retiring last spring, she said she was ready whenever I was, and I took that to mean we were in good shape.”
